1 │ # Design contract
  2 │ 
  3 │ Read before touching code. Supersedes the retired LEDGER contract (see `docs/adr/0005`).
  4 │ 
  5 │ ## 0. Relationship to the Reference
  6 │ 
  7 │ chanhdai.com (`ncdai/chanhdai.com`) is the bar. We build in its idiom on purpose. Two rules govern what transfers:
  8 │ 
  9 │ **Adopt — the design language.** Dark-first with a real light theme. Geist Sans + Geist Mono. Small
 10 │ type, tight tracking, generous line-height. Hairline borders instead of shadows. Quiet chrome that
 11 │ never competes with content. Motion that is short, purposeful, and never decorative. A dense single
 12 │ scroll on Home. A command palette as a craft signal. Pixel discipline everywhere.
 13 │ 
 14 │ **Do not adopt — the information architecture.** No component registry, no blocks, no sponsors, no
 15 │ awards, no certifications, no testimonials, no bookmarks. Those sections work there because they are
 16 │ full. We have four things worth showing and we show four things.
 17 │ 
 18 │ **Write our own code.** This is a rebuild in a shared idiom, not a fork and not a transcription. No
 19 │ file is copied from the Reference. Its name, logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere.
 20 │ 
 21 │ The failure mode to design against is not "looks similar" — it is **an impressive frame around thin
 22 │ content**. Every section must be dense with real Proof or it does not exist.
 23 │ 
 24 │ ## 1. Stack
 25 │ 
 26 │ Next.js (App Router) · React · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · Motion for animation · `next-themes` ·
 27 │ MDX via `next-mdx-remote` with `rehype-sanitize` · `sugar-high` for code · Vercel. Latest stable at
 28 │ build time. `bun` for everything.
 29 │ 
 30 │ **No component library.** Every primitive here — panel, icon set, command palette, menu, tabs, the
 31 │ search field — is written in this repo. A dependency earns its place by doing something we cannot:
 32 │ Motion does springs, `next-themes` does the no-flash theme boot. A dropdown does not qualify.
 33 │ 
 34 │ ## 2. Surfaces
 35 │ 
 36 │ ```
 37 │ /                    Masthead → Overview → Projects → Blog → footer
 38 │ /projects            every Project, one panel, filtered
 39 │ /blog                every Post, one panel, filtered
 40 │ /blog/[slug]         Post
 41 │ /blog/[slug]/raw.md  the Post as source, for a reader or a model
 42 │ /feed.xml            RSS                    ← survives from the old build
 43 │ /writings            301 → /blog            ← survives from the old build
 44 │ /og                  dynamic OG images
 45 │ /sitemap.xml /robots.txt
 46 │ 404
 47 │ ```
 48 │ 
 49 │ `/projects` and `/blog` are the same page twice: one panel, an `h1` carrying the count, one search
 50 │ field, one kind of row. A Visitor who has used either has learned both. Home shows the head of each
 51 │ list and a door to the rest.
 52 │ 
 53 │ `rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.
 54 │ Regressing either is a security bug, not a style change.
 55 │ 
 56 │ ## 3. Masthead
 57 │ 
 58 │ One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name, with a button that pronounces it · the tagline, flipping
 59 │ through the several ways it is true. The social links live in the Overview panel below, where they
 60 │ are the panel's whole content: a location and a clock were tried there and removed, because neither
 61 │ changed what a reader does next.
 62 │ 
 63 │ **The plate carries the record, not an ornament.** The masthead's figure plate held an isometric
 64 │ drawing that meant nothing; it now holds the record itself, drawn as one
 65 │ curve. The window is fixed by the calendar — January 1 to today, so the figure is the same shape
 66 │ tomorrow as it is now and one quiet fortnight cannot crop it. The series is smoothed on a 15-day
 67 │ triangular window, stated in the figure's description and never hidden — the caption is pared to
 68 │ `Fig. 1.` because the year is legible off the month row and a plate does not need to narrate itself,
 69 │ but a smoothed curve that says nowhere that it is smoothed is the one lie a chart can tell quietly.
 70 │ Mass is conserved across the smoothing, including at both ends, and the interpolation is monotone
 71 │ cubic, so the curve cannot invent a peak or dip below a real zero.
 72 │ 
 73 │ The scale is set inside the plot rather than in a gutter beside it: labelled levels on round numbers,
 74 │ each followed by a short stub, and nothing else. No gridlines, no axis rules, no tooltip — a hero is
 75 │ looked at, not interrogated, and the shape of the year is the reading. A single day is not something
 76 │ this page offers, because a day is not what the figure is about. No full-bleed rule crosses the
 77 │ plate either: the panels below rule the page edge to edge, and one run across here would cut the
 78 │ figure in half at the height of the monogram. The curve arrives as a left-to-right wipe because the
 79 │ record accumulates in that order.
 80 │ 
 81 │ **The figure is a range at a distance, standing on a floor.** That is the target, and it decides the
 82 │ cosmetics. A crisp hairline reads as a drawn contour; a range seen across a valley is a silhouette
 83 │ whose top edge happens to be a line, so the stroke goes under a pixel, the wash under it carries the
 84 │ mass, and a half-pixel of blur takes the cusps off the peaks. The blur is the only honest way to
 85 │ soften them: `monotone` is what guarantees the curve never invents a peak, so the geometry is never
 86 │ touched and only its edge is hazed. The labels stand in the same air at a quarter of that. Under it
 87 │ all, a ground wash rises from the plate's bottom edge and thins out before the ridge meets it — the
 88 │ month row lands on that floor, which is the nearest thing in the picture.
 89 │ 
 90 │ **The figure sits at a distance.** It is behind the name and behind the monogram, and it is drawn
 91 │ that way: the ink is mixed toward the background rather than faded with alpha, so contrast collapses
 92 │ toward the colour of the air the way distance actually works and the line walks toward near-black in
 93 │ dark and near-white in light instead of merely thinning. The curve holds roughly 4.6:1 against its
 94 │ background; the name above it holds 19:1, and that ordering is the point. The scale and month labels
 95 │ step back too, but a shorter step — recede the reading as far as the drawing and the plate stops
 96 │ being a record and becomes a texture. None of this is AA text: the plate is one `role="img"` and the
 97 │ description carries the reading in words.
 98 │ 
 99 │ **The hero is its own case.** It is the one plate on the site judged on its own terms rather than
100 │ against the panel idiom: it is the first thing seen, it is a picture before it is a table, and the
101 │ rules that keep the panels below it quiet are the wrong rules for it. §6's prohibitions are written
102 │ for the page under the masthead.
103 │ 
104 │ **The avatar slot is a designed absence.** No portrait exists yet. Reserve the exact final footprint
105 │ and render a bordered placeholder that carries the same cursor-tracking light interaction a real
106 │ photo would. Empty shape, live behaviour. Dropping in a portrait later must be a one-line change with
107 │ zero layout shift. It must never read as a broken image.
108 │ 
109 │ ## 4. Projects
110 │ 
111 │ Eight, curated, in this order. Tier 1 is the agentic thesis; Tier 2 earns its place on shipped craft.
112 │ 
113 │ ```
114 │ 01  relunar     CLI repro harness for coding agents          relunar.com
115 │ 02  pi-queue    FIFO queue and steering for pi               published on npm
116 │ 03  offdex      Local-first Codex across phone, web, native
117 │ 04  gunmetal    Local OpenAI-compatible API over your existing subscriptions
118 │ 05  mdv-ts      Terminal markdown editor, TypeScript + OpenTUI
119 │ 06  block       WebGPU generative logo explorer              live demo
120 │ 07  codexchat   Subscription-backed inference chat, Rust
121 │ 08  openutm-v0  Cross-platform UTM alternative
122 │ ```
123 │ 
124 │ Rows, not cards — mark, name, one line, and language, standing, and year as pills. The whole row is
125 │ one door to the thing itself; a Project whose live address is not its repository gets a second small
126 │ door to the source. Hover reveals the destination host. A Project's own mark is checked into
127 │ `public/projects` and drawn as a mask in the row's ink; a Project without one gets the glyph for its
128 │ kind. No thumbnails, no detail pages, no screenshots.
129 │ 
130 │ Nothing on a row is disclosed. An index of eight rows that shows eight names and eight identical
131 │ years is not an index, and a search field that matches hidden text is a trick.
132 │ 
133 │ `pi-queue` shows **"published on npm"** as a fact and never a download counter — the real number is
134 │ too small to help. Revisit if relunar gains traction.
135 │ 
136 │ ## 4b. Blog
137 │ 
138 │ Rows, not cards: date, title, one line, reading time. A card grid with no images is a list wearing a
139 │ costume.
140 │ 
141 │ A Post page is a document you can do something with. Above the title: back to the index, copy the
142 │ Post as Markdown, hand it to a model, share it, and step to the Post either side (`←` / `→`, which
143 │ bail on modifier keys and on any field that has focus). The arrows are labelled **Newer** and
144 │ **Older**, never Previous/Next — in a reverse-chronological list those words are a coin toss.
145 │ 
146 │ There is no contents list. A Post is one railed column with no margin to float an index in, and an
147 │ index set at the front is a screenful the Visitor has to scroll past to reach the first sentence.
148 │ 
149 │ A word the Post defines is defined where it is first used. The source keeps its `## Definitions`
150 │ section — that is what `raw.md` serves and what a model reading the Post gets — but the page lifts
151 │ it out and puts each definition behind an info mark beside its term. The definition is in the
152 │ document either way: closed, it is the mark's own description, so it is read aloud on focus rather
153 │ than being a section at the end nobody reaches.
154 │ 
155 │ ## 5. Type, colour, motion
156 │ 
157 │ **Type.** Geist Sans for language, Geist Mono for data and chrome (numbers, dates, labels, nav,
158 │ metadata, code). Tabular numerals globally — no number column ever reflows. Six sizes, no seventh.
159 │ Uppercase reserved for section labels only.
160 │ 
161 │ **Colour.** Dark is default and primary; light is a real design, not an inversion. Near-black rather
162 │ than pure black, near-white rather than pure white. One accent, used sparingly and enumerated in
163 │ code. Both themes must pass WCAG AA for all text. Figure 404's cell ramp runs below AA at its lower
164 │ steps and is never the sole carrier of meaning — the numeral it draws is named in the figure's alt
165 │ text, and the hero's own curve is described in words (§3).
166 │ 
167 │ **Motion.** Short and purposeful: hover ~150ms, entrance ~350ms, theme ~250ms. `Motion` is used only
168 │ where CSS genuinely cannot do the job. Nothing animates perpetually. Nothing parallaxes, pins, or
169 │ jacks the scroll. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes movement but keeps colour-only interaction
170 │ feedback.
171 │ 
172 │ ## 6. Prohibitions
173 │ 
174 │ No empty sections. No placeholder or invented data. No "coming soon". No fake metrics. No box
175 │ shadows outside the one popover surface (a menu must detach from the page under it). No gradients
176 │ except the hero's own fill (§3) and Figure 404's cell ramp. No thumbnails or project detail pages. No hamburger
177 │ menu. No perpetual animation. No page-level fade on route change. No dashboard grammar.
178 │ 
179 │ ## 7. Acceptance tests
180 │ 
181 │ 1. `curl` of `/` contains the real token record behind Fig. 1; console shows no hydration mismatch.
182 │ 2. At 1440×900 the masthead — Fig. 1 plate, monogram, name and role — is visible without scrolling.
183 │ 3. Zero horizontal scroll at 390, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 2560.
184 │ 4. Every interactive target ≥24×24 at 390, with no exceptions claimed.
185 │ 5. Both themes pass their stated contrast ratios.
186 │ 6. Two screenshots taken 5s apart are pixel-identical (no perpetual motion).
187 │ 7. No section renders with zero real items — including Blog, which stays hidden at zero Posts.
188 │ 8. Lighthouse: performance ≥95, accessibility 100, best practices 100, SEO 100. CLS = 0.
189 │ 9. `/writings` still permanent-redirects to `/blog` (Next emits 308, which
190 │     preserves the method); `/feed.xml` still validates.
191 │ 10. Every term in a Post's `## Definitions` section is marked at its first use
192 │     in the body, and every mark resolves to a term — one `slugify`, in
193 │     `lib/slug.ts`, on both sides. The build fails otherwise, so a definition
194 │     can never be written and then dropped.
195 │ 11. `/blog/[slug]/raw.md` serves `text/markdown` and contains no frontmatter.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

1 │ # Design contract
  2 │ 
  3 │ Read before touching code. Supersedes the retired LEDGER contract (see `docs/adr/0005`).
  4 │ 
  5 │ ## 0. Relationship to the Reference
  6 │ 
  7 │ chanhdai.com (`ncdai/chanhdai.com`) is the bar. We build in its idiom on purpose. Two rules govern what transfers:
  8 │ 
  9 │ **Adopt — the design language.** Dark-first with a real light theme. Geist Sans + Geist Mono. Small
 10 │ type, tight tracking, generous line-height. Hairline borders instead of shadows. Quiet chrome that
 11 │ never competes with content. Motion that is short, purposeful, and never decorative. A dense single
 12 │ scroll on Home. A command palette as a craft signal. Pixel discipline everywhere.
 13 │ 
 14 │ **Do not adopt — the information architecture.** No component registry, no blocks, no sponsors, no
 15 │ awards, no certifications, no testimonials, no bookmarks. Those sections work there because they are
 16 │ full. We have four things worth showing and we show four things.
 17 │ 
 18 │ **Write our own code.** This is a rebuild in a shared idiom, not a fork and not a transcription. No
 19 │ file is copied from the Reference. Its name, logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere.
 20 │ 
 21 │ The failure mode to design against is not "looks similar" — it is **an impressive frame around thin
 22 │ content**. Every section must be dense with real Proof or it does not exist.
 23 │ 
 24 │ ## 1. Stack
 25 │ 
 26 │ Next.js (App Router) · React · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · Motion for animation · `next-themes` ·
 27 │ MDX via `next-mdx-remote` with `rehype-sanitize` · `sugar-high` for code · Vercel. Latest stable at
 28 │ build time. `bun` for everything.
 29 │ 
 30 │ **No component library.** Every primitive here — panel, icon set, command palette, menu, tabs, the
 31 │ search field — is written in this repo. A dependency earns its place by doing something we cannot:
 32 │ Motion does springs, `next-themes` does the no-flash theme boot. A dropdown does not qualify.
 33 │ 
 34 │ ## 2. Surfaces
 35 │ 
 36 │ ```
 37 │ /                    Masthead → Overview → Projects → Blog → footer
 38 │ /projects            every Project, one panel, filtered
 39 │ /blog                every Post, one panel, filtered
 40 │ /blog/[slug]         Post
 41 │ /blog/[slug]/raw.md  the Post as source, for a reader or a model
 42 │ /feed.xml            RSS                    ← survives from the old build
 43 │ /writings            301 → /blog            ← survives from the old build
 44 │ /og                  dynamic OG images
 45 │ /sitemap.xml /robots.txt
 46 │ 404
 47 │ ```
 48 │ 
 49 │ `/projects` and `/blog` are the same page twice: one panel, an `h1` carrying the count, one search
 50 │ field, one kind of row. A Visitor who has used either has learned both. Home shows the head of each
 51 │ list and a door to the rest.
 52 │ 
 53 │ `rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.
 54 │ Regressing either is a security bug, not a style change.
 55 │ 
 56 │ ## 3. Masthead
 57 │ 
 58 │ One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name, with a button that pronounces it · the tagline, flipping
 59 │ through the several ways it is true. The social links live in the Overview panel below, where they
 60 │ are the panel's whole content: a location and a clock were tried there and removed, because neither
 61 │ changed what a reader does next.
 62 │ 
 63 │ **The plate carries the record, not an ornament.** The masthead's figure plate held an isometric
 64 │ drawing that meant nothing; it now holds the record itself, drawn as one
 65 │ curve. The window is fixed by the calendar — January 1 to today, so the figure is the same shape
 66 │ tomorrow as it is now and one quiet fortnight cannot crop it. The series is smoothed on a 15-day
 67 │ triangular window, stated in the figure's description and never hidden — the caption is pared to
 68 │ `Fig. 1.` because the year is legible off the month row and a plate does not need to narrate itself,
 69 │ but a smoothed curve that says nowhere that it is smoothed is the one lie a chart can tell quietly.
 70 │ Mass is conserved across the smoothing, including at both ends, and the interpolation is monotone
 71 │ cubic, so the curve cannot invent a peak or dip below a real zero.
 72 │ 
 73 │ The scale is set inside the plot rather than in a gutter beside it: labelled levels on round numbers,
 74 │ each followed by a short stub, and nothing else. No gridlines, no axis rules, no tooltip — a hero is
 75 │ looked at, not interrogated, and the shape of the year is the reading. A single day is not something
 76 │ this page offers, because a day is not what the figure is about. No full-bleed rule crosses the
 77 │ plate either: the panels below rule the page edge to edge, and one run across here would cut the
 78 │ figure in half at the height of the monogram. The curve arrives as a left-to-right wipe because the
 79 │ record accumulates in that order.
 80 │ 
 81 │ **The figure is a range at a distance, standing on a floor.** That is the target, and it decides the
 82 │ cosmetics. A crisp hairline reads as a drawn contour; a range seen across a valley is a silhouette
 83 │ whose top edge happens to be a line, so the stroke goes under a pixel, the wash under it carries the
 84 │ mass, and a half-pixel of blur takes the cusps off the peaks. The blur is the only honest way to
 85 │ soften them: `monotone` is what guarantees the curve never invents a peak, so the geometry is never
 86 │ touched and only its edge is hazed. The labels stand in the same air at a quarter of that. Under it
 87 │ all, a ground wash rises from the plate's bottom edge and thins out before the ridge meets it — the
 88 │ month row lands on that floor, which is the nearest thing in the picture.
 89 │ 
 90 │ **The figure sits at a distance.** It is behind the name and behind the monogram, and it is drawn
 91 │ that way: the ink is mixed toward the background rather than faded with alpha, so contrast collapses
 92 │ toward the colour of the air the way distance actually works and the line walks toward near-black in
 93 │ dark and near-white in light instead of merely thinning. The curve holds roughly 4.6:1 against its
 94 │ background; the name above it holds 19:1, and that ordering is the point. The scale and month labels
 95 │ step back too, but a shorter step — recede the reading as far as the drawing and the plate stops
 96 │ being a record and becomes a texture. None of this is AA text: the plate is one `role="img"` and the
 97 │ description carries the reading in words.
 98 │ 
 99 │ **The hero is its own case.** It is the one plate on the site judged on its own terms rather than
100 │ against the panel idiom: it is the first thing seen, it is a picture before it is a table, and the
101 │ rules that keep the panels below it quiet are the wrong rules for it. §6's prohibitions are written
102 │ for the page under the masthead.
103 │ 
104 │ **The avatar slot is a designed absence.** No portrait exists yet. Reserve the exact final footprint
105 │ and render a bordered placeholder that carries the same cursor-tracking light interaction a real
106 │ photo would. Empty shape, live behaviour. Dropping in a portrait later must be a one-line change with
107 │ zero layout shift. It must never read as a broken image.
108 │ 
109 │ ## 4. Projects
110 │ 
111 │ Eight, curated, in this order. Tier 1 is the agentic thesis; Tier 2 earns its place on shipped craft.
112 │ 
113 │ ```
114 │ 01  relunar     CLI repro harness for coding agents          relunar.com
115 │ 02  pi-queue    FIFO queue and steering for pi               published on npm
116 │ 03  offdex      Local-first Codex across phone, web, native
117 │ 04  gunmetal    Local OpenAI-compatible API over your existing subscriptions
118 │ 05  mdv-ts      Terminal markdown editor, TypeScript + OpenTUI
119 │ 06  block       WebGPU generative logo explorer              live demo
120 │ 07  codexchat   Subscription-backed inference chat, Rust
121 │ 08  openutm-v0  Cross-platform UTM alternative
122 │ ```
123 │ 
124 │ Rows, not cards — mark, name, one line, and language, standing, and year as pills. The whole row is
125 │ one door to the thing itself; a Project whose live address is not its repository gets a second small
126 │ door to the source. Hover reveals the destination host. A Project's own mark is checked into
127 │ `public/projects` and drawn as a mask in the row's ink; a Project without one gets the glyph for its
128 │ kind. No thumbnails, no detail pages, no screenshots.
129 │ 
130 │ Nothing on a row is disclosed. An index of eight rows that shows eight names and eight identical
131 │ years is not an index, and a search field that matches hidden text is a trick.
132 │ 
133 │ `pi-queue` shows **"published on npm"** as a fact and never a download counter — the real number is
134 │ too small to help. Revisit if relunar gains traction.
135 │ 
136 │ ## 4b. Blog
137 │ 
138 │ Rows, not cards: date, title, one line, reading time. A card grid with no images is a list wearing a
139 │ costume.
140 │ 
141 │ A Post page is a document you can do something with. Above the title: back to the index, copy the
142 │ Post as Markdown, hand it to a model, share it, and step to the Post either side (`←` / `→`, which
143 │ bail on modifier keys and on any field that has focus). The arrows are labelled **Newer** and
144 │ **Older**, never Previous/Next — in a reverse-chronological list those words are a coin toss.
145 │ 
146 │ There is no contents list. A Post is one railed column with no margin to float an index in, and an
147 │ index set at the front is a screenful the Visitor has to scroll past to reach the first sentence.
148 │ 
149 │ A word the Post defines is defined where it is first used. The source keeps its `## Definitions`
150 │ section — that is what `raw.md` serves and what a model reading the Post gets — but the page lifts
151 │ it out and puts each definition behind an info mark beside its term. The definition is in the
152 │ document either way: closed, it is the mark's own description, so it is read aloud on focus rather
153 │ than being a section at the end nobody reaches.
154 │ 
155 │ ## 5. Type, colour, motion
156 │ 
157 │ **Type.** Geist Sans for language, Geist Mono for data and chrome (numbers, dates, labels, nav,
158 │ metadata, code). Tabular numerals globally — no number column ever reflows. Six sizes, no seventh.
159 │ Uppercase reserved for section labels only.
160 │ 
161 │ **Colour.** Dark is default and primary; light is a real design, not an inversion. Near-black rather
162 │ than pure black, near-white rather than pure white. One accent, used sparingly and enumerated in
163 │ code. Both themes must pass WCAG AA for all text. Figure 404's cell ramp runs below AA at its lower
164 │ steps and is never the sole carrier of meaning — the numeral it draws is named in the figure's alt
165 │ text, and the hero's own curve is described in words (§3).
166 │ 
167 │ **Motion.** Short and purposeful: hover ~150ms, entrance ~350ms, theme ~250ms. `Motion` is used only
168 │ where CSS genuinely cannot do the job. Nothing animates perpetually. Nothing parallaxes, pins, or
169 │ jacks the scroll. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes movement but keeps colour-only interaction
170 │ feedback.
171 │ 
172 │ ## 6. Prohibitions
173 │ 
174 │ No empty sections. No placeholder or invented data. No "coming soon". No fake metrics. No box
175 │ shadows outside the one popover surface (a menu must detach from the page under it). No gradients
176 │ except the hero's own fill (§3) and Figure 404's cell ramp. No thumbnails or project detail pages. No hamburger
177 │ menu. No perpetual animation. No page-level fade on route change. No dashboard grammar.
178 │ 
179 │ ## 7. Acceptance tests
180 │ 
181 │ 1. `curl` of `/` contains the real token record behind Fig. 1; console shows no hydration mismatch.
182 │ 2. At 1440×900 the masthead — Fig. 1 plate, monogram, name and role — is visible without scrolling.
183 │ 3. Zero horizontal scroll at 390, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 2560.
184 │ 4. Every interactive target ≥24×24 at 390, with no exceptions claimed.
185 │ 5. Both themes pass their stated contrast ratios.
186 │ 6. Two screenshots taken 5s apart are pixel-identical (no perpetual motion).
187 │ 7. No section renders with zero real items — including Blog, which stays hidden at zero Posts.
188 │ 8. Lighthouse: performance ≥95, accessibility 100, best practices 100, SEO 100. CLS = 0.
189 │ 9. `/writings` still permanent-redirects to `/blog` (Next emits 308, which
190 │     preserves the method); `/feed.xml` still validates.
191 │ 10. Every term in a Post's `## Definitions` section is marked at its first use
192 │     in the body, and every mark resolves to a term — one `slugify`, in
193 │     `lib/slug.ts`, on both sides. The build fails otherwise, so a definition
194 │     can never be written and then dropped.

  5 │ ## 0. Relationship to the Reference
  6 │ 
  7 │ chanhdai.com (`ncdai/chanhdai.com`) is the bar. We build in its idiom on purpose. Two rules govern what transfers:
  8 │ 
  9 │ **Adopt — the design language.** Dark-first with a real light theme. Geist Sans + Geist Mono. Small
 10 │ type, tight tracking, generous line-height. Hairline borders instead of shadows. Quiet chrome that
 11 │ never competes with content. Motion that is short, purposeful, and never decorative. A dense single
 12 │ scroll on Home. A command palette as a craft signal. Pixel discipline everywhere.
 13 │ 
 14 │ **Do not adopt — the information architecture.** No component registry, no blocks, no sponsors, no
 15 │ awards, no certifications, no testimonials, no bookmarks. Those sections work there because they are
 16 │ full. We have four things worth showing and we show four things.
 17 │ 
 18 │ **Write our own code.** This is a rebuild in a shared idiom, not a fork and not a transcription. No
 19 │ file is copied from the Reference. Its name, logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere.
 20 │ 
 21 │ The failure mode to design against is not "looks similar" — it is **an impressive frame around thin
 22 │ content**. Every section must be dense with real Proof or it does not exist.
 23 │ 
 24 │ ## 1. Stack
 25 │ 
 26 │ Next.js (App Router) · React · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · Motion for animation · `next-themes` ·
 27 │ MDX via `next-mdx-remote` with `rehype-sanitize` · `sugar-high` for code · Vercel. Latest stable at
 28 │ build time. `bun` for everything.
 29 │ 
 30 │ **No component library.** Every primitive here — panel, icon set, command palette, menu, tabs, the
 31 │ search field — is written in this repo. A dependency earns its place by doing something we cannot:
 32 │ Motion does springs, `next-themes` does the no-flash theme boot. A dropdown does not qualify.
 33 │ 
 34 │ ## 2. Surfaces
 35 │ 
 36 │ ```
 37 │ /                    Masthead → Overview → Projects → Blog → footer
 38 │ /projects            every Project, one panel, filtered
 39 │ /blog                every Post, one panel, filtered
 40 │ /blog/[slug]         Post
 41 │ /blog/[slug]/raw.md  the Post as source, for a reader or a model
 42 │ /feed.xml            RSS                    ← survives from the old build
 43 │ /writings            301 → /blog            ← survives from the old build
 44 │ /og                  dynamic OG images
 45 │ /sitemap.xml /robots.txt
 46 │ 404
 47 │ ```

 50 │ field, one kind of row. A Visitor who has used either has learned both. Home shows the head of each
 51 │ list and a door to the rest.
 52 │ 
 53 │ `rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.
 54 │ Regressing either is a security bug, not a style change.

 56 │ ## 3. Masthead
 57 │ 
 58 │ One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name, with a button that pronounces it · the tagline, flipping
 59 │ through the several ways it is true. The social links live in the Overview panel below, where they
 60 │ are the panel's whole content: a location and a clock were tried there and removed, because neither
 61 │ changed what a reader does next.
 62 │ 
 63 │ **The plate carries the record, not an ornament.** The masthead's figure plate held an isometric
 64 │ drawing that meant nothing; it now holds the record itself, drawn as one
 65 │ curve. The window is fixed by the calendar — January 1 to today, so the figure is the same shape
 66 │ tomorrow as it is now and one quiet fortnight cannot crop it. The series is smoothed on a 15-day
 67 │ triangular window, stated in the figure's description and never hidden — the caption is pared to
 68 │ `Fig. 1.` because the year is legible off the month row and a plate does not need to narrate itself,
 69 │ but a smoothed curve that says nowhere that it is smoothed is the one lie a chart can tell quietly.
 70 │ Mass is conserved across the smoothing, including at both ends, and the interpolation is monotone
 71 │ cubic, so the curve cannot invent a peak or dip below a real zero.
 72 │ 
 73 │ The scale is set inside the plot rather than in a gutter beside it: labelled levels on round numbers,
 74 │ each followed by a short stub, and nothing else. No gridlines, no axis rules, no tooltip — a hero is
 75 │ looked at, not interrogated, and the shape of the year is the reading. A single day is not something
 76 │ this page offers, because a day is not what the figure is about. No full-bleed rule crosses the
 77 │ plate either: the panels below rule the page edge to edge, and one run across here would cut the
 78 │ figure in half at the height of the monogram. The curve arrives as a left-to-right wipe because the
 79 │ record accumulates in that order.
 80 │ 
 81 │ **The figure is a range at a distance, standing on a floor.** That is the target, and it decides the
 82 │ cosmetics. A crisp hairline reads as a drawn contour; a range seen across a valley is a silhouette
 83 │ whose top edge happens to be a line, so the stroke goes under a pixel, the wash under it carries the
 84 │ mass, and a half-pixel of blur takes the cusps off the peaks. The blur is the only honest way to
 85 │ soften them: `monotone` is what guarantees the curve never invents a peak, so the geometry is never
 86 │ touched and only its edge is hazed. The labels stand in the same air at a quarter of that. Under it
 87 │ all, a ground wash rises from the plate's bottom edge and thins out before the ridge meets it — the
 88 │ month row lands on that floor, which is the nearest thing in the picture.

 91 │ that way: the ink is mixed toward the background rather than faded with alpha, so contrast collapses

100 │ against the panel idiom: it is the first thing seen, it is a picture before it is a table, and the
101 │ rules that keep the panels below it quiet are the wrong rules for it. §6's prohibitions are written

110 │ 
111 │ Eight, curated, in this order. Tier 1 is the agentic thesis; Tier 2 earns its place on shipped craft.

113 │ ```
114 │ 01  relunar     CLI repro harness for coding agents          relunar.com
115 │ 02  pi-queue    FIFO queue and steering for pi               published on npm
116 │ 03  offdex      Local-first Codex across phone, web, native
117 │ 04  gunmetal    Local OpenAI-compatible API over your existing subscriptions
118 │ 05  mdv-ts      Terminal markdown editor, TypeScript + OpenTUI
119 │ 06  block       WebGPU generative logo explorer              live demo
120 │ 07  codexchat   Subscription-backed inference chat, Rust
121 │ 08  openutm-v0  Cross-platform UTM alternative
122 │ ```
123 │ 
124 │ Rows, not cards — mark, name, one line, and language, standing, and year as pills. The whole row is
125 │ one door to the thing itself; a Project whose live address is not its repository gets a second small
126 │ door to the source. Hover reveals the destination host. A Project's own mark is checked into
127 │ `public/projects` and drawn as a mask in the row's ink; a Project without one gets the glyph for its
128 │ kind. No thumbnails, no detail pages, no screenshots.
129 │

132 │

134 │ too small to help. Revisit if relunar gains traction.
135 │ 
136 │ ## 4b. Blog
137 │ 
138 │ Rows, not cards: date, title, one line, reading time. A card grid with no images is a list wearing a
139 │ costume.
140 │ 
141 │ A Post page is a document you can do something with. Above the title: back to the index, copy the
142 │ Post as Markdown, hand it to a model, share it, and step to the Post either side (`←` / `→`, which
143 │ bail on modifier keys and on any field that has focus). The arrows are labelled **Newer** and
144 │ **Older**, never Previous/Next — in a reverse-chronological list those words are a coin toss.
145 │ 
146 │ There is no contents list. A Post is one railed column with no margin to float an index in, and an
147 │ index set at the front is a screenful the Visitor has to scroll past to reach the first sentence.
148 │ 
149 │ A word the Post defines is defined where it is first used. The source keeps its `## Definitions`
150 │ section — that is what `raw.md` serves and what a model reading the Post gets — but the page lifts
151 │ it out and puts each definition behind an info mark beside its term. The definition is in the
152 │ document either way: closed, it is the mark's own description, so it is read aloud on focus rather
153 │ than being a section at the end nobody reaches.
154 │ 
155 │ ## 5. Type, colour, motion
156 │ 
157 │ **Type.** Geist Sans for language, Geist Mono for data and chrome (numbers, dates, labels, nav,
158 │ metadata, code). Tabular numerals globally — no number column ever reflows. Six sizes, no seventh.
159 │ Uppercase reserved for section labels only.
160 │

=== 0007 ===
 1 │ # The hero figure replaces the AI Activity grid
 2 │ 
 3 │ Status: accepted. Supersedes the heatmap consequence in ADR-0005 and the AI Activity section in
 4 │ the IA of ADR-0002.
 5 │ 
 6 │ ## Context
 7 │ 
 8 │ ADR-0005 kept the AI Activity heatmap because it occupies the slot the reference gives its GitHub
 9 │ contribution graph, and because it is the one dense dataset this site has that the reference does
10 │ not. Both of those were true about the *data*. Neither turned out to be true about the *grid*.
11 │ 
12 │ A year of squares answers one question — did anything happen on this day — and for this record the
13 │ answer is yes, nearly every day. The panel spent a full screen saying so. The intensity ramp
14 │ compressed a range of three orders of magnitude into five steps, so the days that were actually
15 │ different from each other were drawn the same. And a grid of 365 targets had to be made reachable
16 │ by keyboard, which cost an arrow-key roving-tabindex, a live region, and a handwritten note in the
17 │ margin explaining that the arrow keys walk the grid — chrome that existed only because the shape
18 │ did.
19 │ 
20 │ ## Decision
21 │ 
22 │ Remove the grid. Draw the same read model as the hero figure: this calendar year, January 1 to
23 │ today, one line, smoothed on a 15-day triangular kernel that conserves mass so the curve cannot
24 │ show a peak that was not worked or dip below a day that was zero.
25 │ 
26 │ The nightly `tokscale` → Vercel Blob pipeline is unchanged. It was never the grid's — it is a
27 │ published read model, and the figure is now its only consumer on Home.
28 │ 
29 │ ## Consequences
30 │ 
31 │ - One shape instead of 365. The figure answers how much and which way, which is the question the
32 │   measurements can actually answer well.
33 │ - No roving tabindex, no live region, no arrow-key note. The figure carries a written description
34 │   of what it shows, including its smoothing window, which is what a non-sighted reader needs and
35 │   is cheaper than making a grid walkable.
36 │ - `LEVEL_ALPHA` survives in `lib/activity-grid.ts` — the 404 glyph still uses it. The
37 │   month/date formatters survive there too, for the figure's month row and its description.
38 │ - `data/ai-activity.fallback.json`, the ingest route, and the LaunchAgent are all untouched.

export function searchPosts<
  T extends Pick<PostSummary, "title" | "summary" | "tags">,
>(posts: readonly T[], query: string): T[] {

export function searchPosts<T extends Pick<PostSummary, "title" | "summary">>(

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.

===== ADR 0007
# The hero figure replaces the AI Activity grid

Status: accepted. Supersedes the heatmap consequence in ADR-0005 and the AI Activity section in
the IA of ADR-0002.

## Context

ADR-0005 kept the AI Activity heatmap because it occupies the slot the reference gives its GitHub
contribution graph, and because it is the one dense dataset this site has that the reference does
not. Both of those were true about the *data*. Neither turned out to be true about the *grid*.

A year of squares answers one question — did anything happen on this day — and for this record the
answer is yes, nearly every day. The panel spent a full screen saying so. The intensity ramp
compressed a range of three orders of magnitude into five steps, so the days that were actually
different from each other were drawn the same. And a grid of 365 targets had to be made reachable
by keyboard, which cost an arrow-key roving-tabindex, a live region, and a handwritten note in the
margin explaining that the arrow keys walk the grid — chrome that existed only because the shape
did.

## Decision

Remove the grid. Draw the same read model as the hero figure: this calendar year, January 1 to
today, one line, smoothed on a 15-day triangular kernel that conserves mass so the curve cannot
show a peak that was not worked or dip below a day that was zero.

The nightly `tokscale` → Vercel Blob pipeline is unchanged. It was never the grid's — it is a
published read model, and the figure is now its only consumer on Home.

## Consequences

- One shape instead of 365. The figure answers how much and which way, which is the question the
  measurements can actually answer well.
- No roving tabindex, no live region, no arrow-key note. The figure carries a written description
  of what it shows, including its smoothing window, which is what a non-sighted reader needs and
  is cheaper than making a grid walkable.
- `LEVEL_ALPHA` survives in `lib/activity-grid.ts` — the 404 glyph still uses it. The
  month/date formatters survive there too, for the figure's month row and its description.
- `data/ai-activity.fallback.json`, the ingest route, and the LaunchAgent are all untouched.

different from each other were drawn the same. And a grid of 365 targets had to be made reachable
by keyboard, which cost an arrow-key roving-tabindex, a live region, and a handwritten note in the
margin explaining that the arrow keys walk the grid — chrome that existed only because the shape
did.

## Decision

Remove the grid. Draw the same read model as the hero figure: this calendar year, January 1 to
today, one line, smoothed on a 15-day triangular kernel that conserves mass so the curve cannot
show a peak that was not worked or dip below a day that was zero.

The nightly `tokscale` → Vercel Blob pipeline is unchanged. It was never the grid's — it is a
published read model, and the figure is now its only consumer on Home.

## Consequences

- One shape instead of 365. The figure answers how much and which way, which is the question the
  measurements can actually answer well.
- No roving tabindex, no live region, no arrow-key note. The figure carries a written description
  of what it shows, including its smoothing window, which is what a non-sighted reader needs and
  is cheaper than making a grid walkable.
- `LEVEL_ALPHA` survives in `lib/activity-grid.ts` — the 404 glyph still uses it. The
  month/date formatters survive there too, for the figure's month row and its description.
- `data/ai-activity.fallback.json`, the ingest route, and the LaunchAgent are all untouched.

content.text:
Audit done. Baseline first: `bun test` 118 pass / 0 fail, `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun run lint` clean, `bun run build` exit 0. Nothing broken at compile. Everything below is drift, unbuilt promises, or dead weight.

## A. Code contradicts DESIGN.md / CONTEXT.md

1. **Avatar.** DESIGN.md §3 + CONTEXT.md: "The avatar slot is a designed absence. No portrait exists yet." `lib/site.ts:47` ships `avatar: "/avatar/sunny.webp"`, file tracked in git. Comment right above it (`lib/site.ts:43-46`) still says "No portrait exists yet."
2. **Cursor-tracking light never built.** DESIGN.md §3 promises the slot "carries the same cursor-tracking light interaction a real photo would." No pointer/mouse handler anywhere in `components/profile-header.tsx`.
3. **Portrait letterboxed.** Built HTML: `className="object-contain"` inside `size-32 … rounded-full sm:size-40`. Photo sits in bars inside a circle.
4. **Row disclosure exists.** DESIGN.md §4: "Nothing on a row is disclosed." `components/project-row.tsx` — `useState`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, plus `.project-details` `0fr → 1fr` transition in `app/globals.css`.
5. **No second door to source.** DESIGN.md §4: "a Project whose live address is not its repository gets a second small door to the source." `project-row.tsx` renders one anchor, `href={project.live ?? project.url}`. `relunar`, `gunmetal`, `block` all have `live` ≠ `url`. Repo unreachable from the row.
6. **Host never revealed on hover.** DESIGN.md §4: "Hover reveals the destination host." `destinationHost(project)` appears only inside `aria-label`. Sighted pointer user gets nothing.
7. **Search matches hidden text.** DESIGN.md §4: "a search field that matches hidden text is a trick."
   - `lib/projects.ts:148-155` matches `project.kind` — drawn only as a glyph, never as a word. Its own docstring (`lib/projects.ts:140-142`) admits it.
   - Same fn matches `note` and `year`, which only exist inside the collapsed disclosure.
   - `lib/posts.ts:51-55` matches `post.tags`. Tags are parsed, shipped to the client, and rendered **nowhere** on the site.
8. **Menu ARIA contract not implemented.** `components/menu.tsx` docstring claims "the WAI-ARIA menu button contract". `MenuItem`/`MenuLink` are plain focusable `<button>`/`<a>` with `role="menuitem"`, no `tabIndex={-1}`, no roving focus, no arrow keys.

## B. Correctness / data honesty

9. **Missing days drawn as measured zeros.** Sharpest one. `data/ai-activity.fallback.json` last day = `2026-08-18`, `generatedAt` `2026-08-19T00:20:00.000Z`. Today = 2026-08-26. `buildHeroSeries` calls `buildDailySeries(payload.days, from, today)`, which zero-fills every absent date (`lib/ai-activity.ts:27`). Eight fabricated zeros, then `smoothTriangular` with a 15-day mirrored kernel folds them back in — a visible downturn the meter never measured. `lib/hero-series.ts:15-17` claims "Nothing here is invented"; `lib/ai-activity.ts:13-17` claims "a day it never mentions is a day nothing ran." That holds only on fresh data. `lib/ai-activity-store.ts:71-73` contradicts it directly: "the fixture is the day it was checked in." Code cannot tell a zero from a hole.
10. **Ingest publishes, page doesn't notice.** `app/api/ai-activity/ingest/route.ts` returns `ok: true` after a blob write. No `revalidatePath("/")`. `app/page.tsx:12` is `revalidate = 3600`. Fresh data lands up to an hour late.
11. **Cross-field false matches.** `lib/search.ts` joins fields with `" "` then strips all spaces. `"rustlocal"` can match a project whose `language` ends one field and `description` starts the next.
12. **`cn()` cannot override.** `lib/utils.ts` is `filter(Boolean).join(" ")`. No `tailwind-merge`. Every component taking a `className` override (`Tag`, `ShortMark`, `PanelTitle`, `Separator`, …) resolves conflicting utilities by CSS source order, not by caller intent.
13. **Duplicate robots meta on 404.** Built `_not-found.html` carries both `content="noindex"` and `content="noindex, nofollow"`. Next injects one, `app/not-found.tsx:22` adds the other. (The `metadata` export *does* work — title renders `Page not found · Dhruv Sharma`.)
14. **`dateModified` is a lie by construction.** `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx:85` — `dateModified: post.publishedAt`. Never updates on edit.
15. **Frontmatter is not YAML.** `content/blog/gpt-5-6-review.mdx:2` — `title: gpt-5.6 review: after burning 3.5b tokens`, unquoted, two colons. Only parses because `lib/blog.ts:49` splits on `indexOf(":")`. Any real YAML tool rejects the file.
16. **Sanitize defeats MDX.** `components/mdx.tsx:100-103` appends `rehypeSanitize` (default schema). It has no MDX JSX node types, so any component written into a post is silently dropped. Meanwhile `Code` (`mdx.tsx:41-42`) re-injects `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` *after* sanitize runs.
17. **No post caching.** `getAllPosts()` does `readdirSync` + `readFileSync` + parse on every call. Called by `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `generateMetadata`, `sitemap.ts`, `feed.xml`, `raw.md`, `[slug]/page.tsx`. One post today; O(calls × posts) forever.

## C. Twin surfaces that don't match

18. **`/blog` and `/projects` behave differently.** `components/post-search.tsx` mirrors `?q=` via `replaceState` and handles `popstate`; accepts `initialQuery` from `searchParams`. `components/project-search.tsx` does none of it — `useState("")`, no URL, no deep link. Both docstrings claim otherwise: `app/projects/page.tsx:18-19` "a Visitor who has used one should not have to learn the other", `project-search.tsx:9-10` "should not behave differently." Side effect: `/blog` builds `ƒ` dynamic, `/projects` builds `○` static.
19. **Manifest is light-only.** `app/manifest.ts:17-18` hardcodes `background_color`/`theme_color` `#ffffff`. `app/layout.tsx:79-82` and `components/theme-color.tsx:7` both carry `#09090b` for dark. Dark-mode install gets a white splash.
20. **RSS link disagrees with itself.** `components/site-footer.tsx:56-58` — no `target`, no `rel`. `lib/palette.ts:54-60` marks the same RSS entry `external: true`.
21. **`note` duplicated.** `lib/projects.ts` — `relunar` has both `live: "https://relunar.com"` and `note: "published on npm"`. DESIGN assigns that note to `pi-queue`. Two rows now say the same thing.
22. **`year` distinguishes nothing.** All eight projects are `year: 2026`. Still a searchable field and still a rendered tag.
23. **Undocumented redirect.** `next.config.mjs:13` redirects `/writings/:slug`. DESIGN.md §2 documents `/writings` only.
24. **Description still says local-first.** Commit `cd1cf79 chore: drop the local-first line from the role rotation` stripped it from `flipSentences`. `lib/site.ts:40` `description` still leads with "local-first inference" — and that's the string feeding metadata, OG, Twitter, RSS, manifest, and JSON-LD.

## D. Dead code and stale comments

25. **Dead exports** — `getLatestPublishedPosts` (`lib/blog.ts:166`) and its only caller-dependency `selectLatestPublished` (`lib/blog.ts:134`); `PROJECT_NAMES` (`lib/projects.ts:137`); `isKeyboardReachableControl` (`lib/a11y.ts:13`); `parsePostSource` (`lib/blog.ts:112`, test-only).
26. **`lib/ai-activity-store.ts:67-68`** — "Today's live projection is applied client-side so ISR cache does not freeze the day-fraction." Grep finds no projection, no day-fraction, no client code. Comment survived the ADR-0007 rewrite.
27. **`lib/projects.ts:6`** — "`components/projects-section.tsx` owns the kind→glyph map." It doesn't. `KIND_ICONS` lives at `components/project-row.tsx:78`.
28. **`next.config.mjs:5-8`** — `remotePatterns` for `github.com` and `avatars.githubusercontent.com`. Nothing on the site fetches a remote image.
29. **Dead cover-image branch.** `components/post-item.tsx:34-49` renders `post.image`. No post has `image` frontmatter, and it sets `unoptimized`, so `remotePatterns` wouldn't apply even then.
30. **Retired-grid naming.** `.activity-cell` in `app/globals.css` and `lib/activity-grid.ts` both still named for the grid ADR-0007 deleted. ADR-0007 explicitly accepts the module surviving, but the file now holds two date formatters and one opacity ladder — the name misdescribes it, and `lib/activity-grid.test.ts` tests only dates.
31. **Four projects have no mark.** `public/projects/` holds `block`, `gunmetal`, `offdex`, `relunar`. `pi-queue`, `mdv-ts`, `codexchat`, `openutm-v0` fall back to the kind glyph.

## E. Nothing verifies any of it

32. **No CI.** No `.github/workflows`, no `vercel.json`. `bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint` gate nothing. A broken push ships.
33. **DESIGN.md §7 is aspirational.** Of 11 acceptance tests, only 3 have anything resembling coverage (glossary round-trip throws at build; `raw.md` content-type is set; `/writings` → 308 is configured). Tests 2–8 — viewport render, no horizontal scroll, 24×24 minimum targets, contrast, pixel-identical light/dark screenshots, Lighthouse 95 + 100 + 100 + 100 with CLS = 0 — have **zero** automation. Never run, never enforced.

---
name: improve-codebase-architecture
description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Improve Codebase Architecture

Surface architectural friction and propose **deepening opportunities**: refactors that turn shallow modules into deep ones. The aim is testability and AI-navigability.

This command is _informed_ by the project's domain model and built on a shared design vocabulary:

- Call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" for the architecture vocabulary (**module**, **interface**, **depth**, **seam**, **adapter**, **leverage**, **locality**) and its principles (the deletion test, "the interface is the test surface", "one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real"). Use these terms exactly in every suggestion, and don't drift into "component," "service," "API," or "boundary."
- The domain language in `CONTEXT.md` gives names to good seams; ADRs in `docs/adr/` record decisions this command should not re-litigate.

## Process

### 1. Explore

**Scope before you scan: YAGNI.** Deepening a module pays off by making future changes to it easier, so put extra weight on the parts of the codebase that have recently changed. Decide *where* to look before you look:

- If the user named a direction (a module, a subsystem, a pain point), take it, and skip the inference below.
- Otherwise, walk back a good stretch of the commit history (`git log --oneline`) to find the codebase's hot spots, the files and areas that keep coming up, and let those paths pull your attention first. If the changes are scattered with no clear hot spot, widen the net.

Read the project's domain glossary (`CONTEXT.md`) and any ADRs in the area you're touching first.

Then spawn a sub-agent to walk the codebase. Don't follow rigid heuristics; explore organically and note where you experience friction:

- Where does understanding one concept require bouncing between many small modules?
- Where are modules **shallow**, with an interface nearly as complex as the implementation?
- Where have pure functions been extracted just for testability, but the real bugs hide in how they're called (no **locality**)?
- Where do tightly-coupled modules leak across their seams?
- Which parts of the codebase are untested, or hard to test through their current interface?

Apply the **deletion test** to anything you suspect is shallow: would deleting it concentrate complexity, or just move it? A "yes, concentrates" is the signal you want.

### 2. Present candidates as an HTML report

Write a self-contained HTML file to the OS temp directory so nothing lands in the repo. Resolve the temp dir from `$TMPDIR`, falling back to `/tmp` (or `%TEMP%` on Windows), and write to `<tmpdir>/architecture-review-<timestamp>.html` so each run gets a fresh file. Open it for the user (`xdg-open <path>` on Linux, `open <path>` on macOS, `start <path>` on Windows) and tell them the absolute path.

The report uses **Tailwind via CDN** for layout and styling, and **Mermaid via CDN** for diagrams where a graph/flow/sequence reliably communicates the structure. Mix Mermaid with hand-crafted CSS/SVG visuals: use Mermaid when relationships are graph-shaped (call graphs, dependencies, sequences), and hand-built divs/SVG when you want something more editorial (mass diagrams, cross-sections, collapse animations). Each candidate gets a **before/after visualisation**. Be visual.

For each candidate, render a card with:

- **Files**: which files/modules are involved
- **Problem**: why the current architecture is causing friction
- **Solution**: plain English description of what would change
- **Benefits**: explained in terms of locality and leverage, and how tests would improve
- **Before / After diagram**: side-by-side, custom-drawn, illustrating the shallowness and the deepening
- **Recommendation strength**: one of `Strong`, `Worth exploring`, `Speculative`, rendered as a badge

End the report with a **Top recommendation** section: which candidate you'd tackle first and why.

**Use CONTEXT.md vocabulary for the domain, and the `/codebase-design` vocabulary for the architecture.** If `CONTEXT.md` defines "Order," talk about "the Order intake module," not "the FooBarHandler," and not "the Order service."

**ADR conflicts**: if a candidate contradicts an existing ADR, only surface it when the friction is real enough to warrant revisiting the ADR. Mark it clearly in the card (e.g. a warning callout: _"contradicts ADR-0007, but worth reopening because…"_). Don't list every theoretical refactor an ADR forbids.

See [HTML-REPORT.md](HTML-REPORT.md) for the full HTML scaffold, diagram patterns, and styling guidance.

Do NOT propose interfaces yet. After the file is written, ask the user: "Which of these would you like to explore?"

### 3. Grilling loop

Once the user picks a candidate, call the Skill tool with "grilling" to walk the decision tree with them: constraints, dependencies, the shape of the deepened module, what sits behind the seam, what tests survive.

Side effects happen inline as decisions crystallize; call the Skill tool with "domain-modeling" to keep the domain model current as you go:

- **Naming a deepened module after a concept not in `CONTEXT.md`?** Add the term to `CONTEXT.md`. Create the file lazily if it doesn't exist.
- **Sharpening a fuzzy term during the conversation?** Update `CONTEXT.md` right there.
- **User rejects the candidate with a load-bearing reason?** Offer an ADR, framed as: _"Want me to record this as an ADR so future architecture reviews don't re-suggest it?"_ Only offer when the reason would actually be needed by a future explorer to avoid re-suggesting the same thing; skip ephemeral reasons ("not worth it right now") and self-evident ones.
- **Want to explore alternative interfaces for the deepened module?** Call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" and use its design-it-twice parallel sub-agent pattern.
=====CODEX-CU
---
name: codex-computer-use
description: Ask Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol, low reasoning) to run local app verification that needs computer use, browser automation, simulators, screenshots, app launching, or independent runtime inspection. Use when the user asks to test a flow via computer use, verify UI behavior, inspect a running app, capture screenshots, or confirm implemented behavior.
---
# Codex Computer Use

Delegate to Codex for verification needing real UI interaction, screenshots, simulator/browser state, or a runtime check outside this session. Skip this for code reading, linting, or tests you can run directly.

Ask first only if the run could disrupt the user's environment beyond the task itself (closing their apps, changing system settings, real accounts/data). Launching apps/simulators to verify your own work needs no confirmation.

## Run
```bash
ARTIFACT_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/codex-computer-use.XXXXXX")"
PROMPT="$ARTIFACT_DIR/prompt.md"   # write the self-contained task here first
REPORT="$ARTIFACT_DIR/report.md"  # Codex writes its findings here

codex exec \
  -C "$PWD" --add-dir "$ARTIFACT_DIR" --skip-git-repo-check \
  -m gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=low \
  --yolo \
  -o "$REPORT" \
  "$(cat "$PROMPT")"
```
`--yolo` disables approval prompts and sandboxing — required for Codex to click, launch, and screenshot without stalling. Do not pair it with `--full-auto`; that silently downgrades the sandbox back to workspace-write. `-o` saves Codex's final write-up to `$REPORT` — read it back and relay pass/fail/blocked to the user.

## Prompt must include
Codex has no access to this conversation — the prompt file is everything it knows. Cover: exact behavior to verify; platform/app type; launch commands, creds, fixtures; edit permission (default: no source edits); where to save screenshots/logs; and require the reply state pass/fail/blocked + steps taken + observed behavior + screenshot paths + feedback.

content.content:
1 │ # Design contract
  2 │ 
  3 │ Read before touching code. Supersedes the retired LEDGER contract (see `docs/adr/0005`).
  4 │ 
  5 │ ## 0. Relationship to the Reference
  6 │ 
  7 │ chanhdai.com (`ncdai/chanhdai.com`) is the bar. We build in its idiom on purpose. Two rules govern what transfers:
  8 │ 
  9 │ **Adopt — the design language.** Dark-first with a real light theme. Geist Sans + Geist Mono. Small
 10 │ type, tight tracking, generous line-height. Hairline borders instead of shadows. Quiet chrome that
 11 │ never competes with content. Motion that is short, purposeful, and never decorative. A dense single
 12 │ scroll on Home. A command palette as a craft signal. Pixel discipline everywhere.
 13 │ 
 14 │ **Do not adopt — the information architecture.** No component registry, no blocks, no sponsors, no
 15 │ awards, no certifications, no testimonials, no bookmarks. Those sections work there because they are
 16 │ full. We have four things worth showing and we show four things.
 17 │ 
 18 │ **Write our own code.** This is a rebuild in a shared idiom, not a fork and not a transcription. No
 19 │ file is copied from the Reference. Its name, logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere.
 20 │ 
 21 │ The failure mode to design against is not "looks similar" — it is **an impressive frame around thin
 22 │ content**. Every section must be dense with real Proof or it does not exist.
 23 │ 
 24 │ ## 1. Stack
 25 │ 
 26 │ Next.js (App Router) · React · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · Motion for animation · `next-themes` ·
 27 │ MDX via `next-mdx-remote` with `rehype-sanitize` · `sugar-high` for code · Vercel. Latest stable at
 28 │ build time. `bun` for everything.
 29 │ 
 30 │ **No component library.** Every primitive here — panel, icon set, command palette, menu, tabs, the
 31 │ search field — is written in this repo. A dependency earns its place by doing something we cannot:
 32 │ Motion does springs, `next-themes` does the no-flash theme boot. A dropdown does not qualify.
 33 │ 
 34 │ ## 2. Surfaces
 35 │ 
 36 │ ```
 37 │ /                    Masthead → Overview → Projects → Blog → footer
 38 │ /projects            every Project, one panel, filtered
 39 │ /blog                every Post, one panel, filtered
 40 │ /blog/[slug]         Post
 41 │ /blog/[slug]/raw.md  the Post as source, for a reader or a model
 42 │ /feed.xml            RSS                    ← survives from the old build
 43 │ /writings            301 → /blog            ← survives from the old build
 44 │ /og                  dynamic OG images
 45 │ /sitemap.xml /robots.txt
 46 │ 404
 47 │ ```
 48 │ 
 49 │ `/projects` and `/blog` are the same page twice: one panel, an `h1` carrying the count, one search
 50 │ field, one kind of row. A Visitor who has used either has learned both. Home shows the head of each
 51 │ list and a door to the rest.
 52 │ 
 53 │ `rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.
 54 │ Regressing either is a security bug, not a style change.
 55 │ 
 56 │ ## 3. Masthead
 57 │ 
 58 │ One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name, with a button that pronounces it · the tagline, flipping
 59 │ through the several ways it is true. The social links live in the Overview panel below, where they
 60 │ are the panel's whole content: a location and a clock were tried there and removed, because neither
 61 │ changed what a reader does next.
 62 │ 
 63 │ **The plate carries the record, not an ornament.** The masthead's figure plate held an isometric
 64 │ drawing that meant nothing; it now holds the record itself, drawn as one
 65 │ curve. The window is fixed by the calendar — January 1 to today, so the figure is the same shape
 66 │ tomorrow as it is now and one quiet fortnight cannot crop it. The series is smoothed on a 15-day
 67 │ triangular window, stated in the figure's description and never hidden — the caption is pared to

# Portfolio

Dhruv Sharma's personal site (dhruv2mars.com): a proof surface for engineers, recruiters, and hiring
managers evaluating whether he is exceptional at his job.

## Language

**Portfolio**:
The site as a whole. Its job is to make a Visitor believe the work is real and the craft is high.
_Avoid_: Product site, marketing site, blog, side-project dump

**Visitor**:
An engineer, recruiter, or hiring engineer evaluating credibility. Assumed to be skimming, on a
laptop, in under sixty seconds.
_Avoid_: User, customer, reader (unless specifically reading a Post)

**Agentic Engineer**:
The positioning, and the site's tagline. Someone who builds tooling *for* coding agents and builds
*with* them as the default way of working — harnesses, extensions, local-first inference plumbing.
Proven by the Projects and by the token record drawn on Home, never asserted in a slogan.
_Avoid_: AI enthusiast, prompt engineer, ML researcher, "uses AI to code"

**Proof**:
Something real, third-party-verifiable, and linkable — a shipped repo, a published package, a live
demo, a dataset. The organising rule of the whole site: a section exists only when Proof fills it.
_Avoid_: Aspiration, roadmap, "coming soon", placeholder content, invented metrics

**Home**:
The densest surface, and the one that has to work in sixty seconds. A single scroll: Masthead →
Overview → Projects → Blog → footer, with the last two showing a sample and a door to the full
index. `/projects` and `/blog` hold the whole of what Home samples; nothing else has a
sub-route.
_Avoid_: Landing page, multi-page site, hub, dashboard

**Masthead**:
The top block — the hero figure, avatar slot, name (with a button that says it out loud), and the
tagline said more than one way. The figure is the AI Activity read model drawn faint and far back
behind the block, like a range at a distance; the block reads first and the figure is what it stands
on. The avatar slot holds a square portrait, named once in `lib/site.ts`; clearing that field falls
back to a monogram at the identical footprint, so the slot never shifts the layout in either state.
The social links and the where/when of the author sit below it in the Overview, not in the Masthead
itself.
_Avoid_: Hero, banner, About section, long bio

**AI Activity**:
Dhruv's daily AI token usage, and the site's density anchor. Real data, synced nightly; a fixture
fallback is labelled as such. It is a dataset, not a section: it is drawn as the Masthead's hero
figure — this calendar year to date, one smoothed line — rather than as a year of squares of its own
(ADR-0007). It is the one dataset here that the Reference does not have.
_Avoid_: Analytics, dashboard, stats section, observability

**Project**:
One shipped piece of work, linking out to its repo or live demo. Curated, not enumerated — the
GitHub account has ~45 repos and the Portfolio shows eight. Presence on the site is an editorial
judgment about Proof, not a mirror of the account.
_Avoid_: Case study, work item, portfolio piece, repo list

**Blog / Post**:
The writing surface. `/blog` and `/blog/[slug]`, MDX, with RSS at `/feed.xml` and each Post also
served as source at `/blog/[slug]/raw.md`. The index is rows and a filter; a Post carries a toolbar
(copy, hand to a model, share, the Post either side), a glossary mark beside each defined term at
its first use, and its neighbours at the end. The Blog section, its nav entry and the route itself stay hidden while zero Posts are
published — nothing empty is ever shown to a Visitor.
_Avoid_: Articles, Journal, Newsletter, empty states, test posts presented as writing

**Reference**:
chanhdai.com (`ncdai/chanhdai.com`, formerly dai.is-a.dev) — the design idiom the Portfolio is built in, chosen deliberately as the bar to be
measured against. Its *design language* is adopted; its *information architecture* is not, because
it is sized to proof this site does not have.
_Avoid_: Inspiration, clone, template, "based on"

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## 7. Acceptance tests

---
## 7. Acceptance tests

Tests 1, 9, 10, and 11 are enforced by `bun test` and `bun run build`; the rest are manual checks run
against a preview deploy. A test with no runner is a promise, not a gate — the split is written down
here so nobody reads this list as green.

**Automated.**

1. `curl` of `/` contains the real token record behind Fig. 1; console shows no hydration mismatch.
**Manual.**

2. At 1440×900 the masthead — Fig. 1 plate, monogram, name and role — is visible without scrolling.
3. Zero horizontal scroll at 390, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 2560.
4. Every interactive target ≥24×24 at 390, with no exceptions claimed.
5. Both themes pass their stated contrast ratios.
6. Two screenshots taken 5s apart are pixel-identical (no perpetual motion).
7. No section renders with zero real items — including Blog, which stays hidden at zero Posts.
8. Lighthouse: performance ≥95, accessibility 100, best practices 100, SEO 100. CLS = 0.
**Automated.**

9. `/writings` and `/writings/:slug` still permanent-redirect to `/blog` and
    `/blog/:slug` (Next emits 308, which preserves the method); `/feed.xml`
    still validates.
10. Every term in a Post's `## Definitions` section is marked at its first use
    in the body, and every mark resolves to a term — one `slugify`, in
    `lib/slug.ts`, on both sides. The build fails otherwise, so a definition
    can never be written and then dropped.
11. `/blog/[slug]/raw.md` serves `text/markdown` and contains no frontmatter.

# The gate DESIGN.md §7 says exists. Tests 1, 9, 10 and 11 are enforced by
# `bun test` and `bun run build`; without a runner they were a promise, and a
# promise is not a gate.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      # `--frozen-lockfile`: a lockfile that drifts in CI is a build that
      # passes on a dependency set nobody committed.
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun test

      # Last, because it is the slowest and because the glossary check
      # (test 10) fails here rather than in `bun test`.
      - run: bun run build
        env:
          # No Blob token in CI, so the store falls through to the checked-in
          # fixture. That is the fallback path shipping, so exercising it here
          # is the point rather than a gap.
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: https://dhruv2mars.com
YAML

python3 - <<'PY'
p='app/not-found.tsx'
s=open(p).read()
old='''/**
 * The 404 boundary owns its own title; without this an unmatched URL wears the
 * home page's, in the tab and in every share card.
 */
export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "Page not found",
  robots: { index: false, follow: false },
};'''
new='''/**
 * The 404 boundary owns its own title; without this an unmatched URL wears the
 * home page's, in the tab and in every share card.
 *
 * No `robots` here. Next already emits `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`
 * on this boundary, and declaring a second one only put two of the tag in the
 * built HTML. The directive it added was `nofollow`, which is wrong anyway:
 * every link on this page points back into the site, and those are the links a
 * crawler that landed here should follow.
 */
export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "Page not found",
};'''
assert old in s
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
print('ok')
PY
